questions.q: In 'The Owl and the Grasshopper', why was the old Owl upset with the Grasshopper?
choices: His singing woke her from her daytime sleep
questions.evidence: leave me to sleep in quiet

questions.q: In 'The Owl and the Grasshopper', how did the Owl trick the Grasshopper?
choices: She flattered him and invited him to taste her wine
She asked him to teach her to sing
questions.evidence: The foolish Grasshopper was taken in by the Owl's flattering words.

questions.q: What is a lesson of 'The Owl and the Grasshopper'?
choices: Do not let flattery throw you off guard against an enemy
Always sing as loud as you can
questions.evidence: Do not let flattery throw you off your guard against an enemy.

questions.q: In 'The Wolf and His Shadow', why did the Wolf think he was bigger than a Lion?
choices: The setting sun made his shadow look huge
He had eaten a big dinner
He saw his reflection in a pond
questions.evidence: the setting sun cast his shadow far out on the ground

questions.q: In 'The Oak and the Reeds', what did the Reeds do when the wind blew?
choices: They bowed low so they would not break
They stood up straight and tall
questions.evidence: We bow before them and so we do not break.

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Oak and the Reeds'?
choices: Better to yield than to resist stubbornly and be destroyed
questions.evidence: Better to yield when it is folly to resist

questions.q: In 'The Rat and the Elephant', why was the Rat's pride hurt?
choices: Everyone admired the Elephant and nobody noticed him
questions.evidence: the Rat was not noticed. His pride was hurt.

questions.q: In 'The Rat and the Elephant', what happened while the Rat was bragging?
choices: The crowd started cheering for him
The King invited him to ride along
